quote: we train a new model, called DREAM, to specifically answer these elaboration questions

We train a T5-11B model for scene elaboration, DREAM, starting with the Macaw checkpoint and by using the Scene Elaborations Dataset ... The output is the scene elaboration SE (a 4‑tuple {M, E, ROT, Con})
We train a T5-11B model for scene elaboration, DREAM, starting with the Macaw checkpoint and by using the Scene Elaborations Dataset (Section 4.1).
outputs: Scene elaborations (a 4-tuple of text: motivation, emotion, rule of thumb, consequence)
scene elaborations in the form of a 4-tuple {M, E, ROT, Con} with textual descriptions along dimensions of motivation, emotion, rule of thumb, and consequence

quote: We use human evaluation using (mechanical Turk) crowdworkers.

Workers rate each of the four components (each typically a sentence) of the scene elaboration along 2 dimensions: SE accuracy ... SE usefulness ... SE consistency ... We collect and average three worker scores for each question.
We use human evaluation using (mechanical Turk) crowdworkers.
guideline: Workers rate each of the four components of the scene elaboration along 2 dimensions: SE accuracy and SE usefulness. Each component gets a score of 1 (yes) / 0.5 (a bit) / 0 (no). Also, workers rate the complete SE along SE consistency, measuring the fraction of sentences consistent with each other.
Annotators were asked to rate each component for accuracy (true/false), usefulness (helps answer the question), and the whole elaboration for consistency with itself.
Workers rate each of the four components of the scene elaboration along 2 dimensions: SE accuracy and SE usefulness. In addition, workers rate the complete SE along the dimension of SE consistency.
